main_text.p: dem, ne insequatur, ab imminenti periculo liberatus, nihilominus illi necem intentaverit, non solum non tutus erit in conscientia, verum etiam in foro soli in culpa constituetur, arbitraria poena puniendus, ut qui legitimae defensionis modum excesserit.
main_text.head: CAP. XX. Defensio necessaria utrum licita adversus Magistratum?
main_text.p: Clar. §.Defensio sui ipsius, quæ cum moderamine sic[?] tu-telae inculpatae Homicidium. n. 29.rabilis, ut concessa sit cuivis adversus quemvis, servo adversus dominum, Vasallo adversus seniorem, liberto adversus patronum, filio adversus parentem; quinimo subditis adversus superiores. Neque quispiam in conscientia deli-

page.notes: Marginal notes, left side, in order: "Clar. §."; "Homicidium. n. 29." (printed as "Homici- / dium. n. / 29."); "Berlich. part. 4."; "Concl. 12. n. 29."; "30. Leff. de just. & jur. l."; "2. cap. 9."; "dub. 8."; "Obrecht. tract. de". The printed "Leff." is doubtful (could be "Lefs."). The word "sic" after "moderamine" is doubtful and the sense of "sic tu-telae" is unclear. The body paragraph is set with the first word "Defensio" under a large initial D. The last note "Obrecht. tract. de" is the printed reference beside the final line, and the remaining note lines are placed where they stand beside the text. The catchword "quisse" is at the lower right; the text ends with "deli-" on the last full line.
